findings.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full safeParse result, causing Google refreshes to store { success, data } instead of OAuth credentials and corrupt the credential
refreshOAuthTokens sync branch always returns a Fetch Response, which is incompatible with the response types expected by Google, HubSpot, Zoho, and Bigin and can cause crashes or undefined tokens
Credential-sync requests include only a user ID and app slug without authentication, potentially allowing external callers to obtain OAuth tokens for arbitrary users and integrations
Computed Zod object keys do not create wildcard properties, so token fields such as expires_in and expiry_date are stripped, causing invalid credentials or repeated refreshes
Zoho Bigin passes credentialId to refreshOAuthTokens instead of the required Cal.com user ID, causing incorrect credential lookup or failed refreshes
Salesforce bypasses refreshOAuthTokens and sends the stored refresh token directly to Salesforce, which fails when sync-managed credentials contain only a placeholder refresh token
Salesforce refreshes its token unconditionally during service construction even when the access token is valid, adding latency and risking OAuth token-limit exhaustion
The webhook performs a race-prone findFirst followed by create, allowing concurrent deliveries or retries to create duplicate credentials for the same user and app
Webhook validation, decryption, and JSON parsing errors are uncaught, causing malformed requests to return HTTP 500 instead of a client error and triggering unnecessary retries

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Credential-sync requests include only a user ID and app slug without authentication, potentially allowing external callers to obtain OAuth tokens for arbitrary users and integrations

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the refreshOAuthTokens function in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, it makes a POST request to the external endpoint with only calcomUserId and appSlug in the body. There is no authentication header or secret being sent with this outbound request. This means the external credential sync endpoint receives requests without any verification that they came from the Cal.com instance. However, this is an OUTBOUND request from Cal.com to an external service - the external service is responsible for its own authentication. The finding seems to confuse this with the INBOUND webhook at /api/webhook/app-credential which DOES have proper authentication via CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET. The outbound request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is controlled by the self-hoster who configures both endpoints, so they would configure their own authentication on their endpoint. This is not a security vulnerability in the Cal.com code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The webhook performs a race-prone findFirst followed by create, allowing concurrent deliveries or retries to create duplicate credentials for the same user and app

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the webhook handler in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts, lines 56-90 show a findFirst query followed by either an update or create operation. If two concurrent webhook requests arrive for the same userId and appSlug, both could execute findFirst before either completes the create, resulting in duplicate credentials. This is a real race condition - the code does `findFirst` to check if credential exists, then separately does `create` if not found. There's no transaction or unique constraint enforcement shown that would prevent this. This is a classic TOCTOU (time-of-check-time-of-use) race condition that could result in duplicate credential records.
